schema.description: A note in the person's own words, and since v2 (card 104) an edge: a fact that joins facets, with or without words. `from` and `to` are each a list of facet ids and `kind` says what the join means; a note about some facets is an edge of kind `about` with no `from`, the kind every v1 value has. The facets it names are never changed by it; the edge is appended beside them, carries its own provenance (the person, typed, or the conversation that took it down, or a model's reading), and is retracted or edited on its own. Its fact time is the moment it was asserted (v2 of note.annotation, 2026-10-13): the one time nothing else holds, since each facet it names carries its own fact time, and anam-time is the ingest, not the writing. Which version of each named facet was current when the edge landed is read from the ledger at that watermark, not stored here; `pins` may name the exact version where that matters. A value carries words, ends, or both: `text` alone is an account that names nothing yet (card 157), a later version of the same id can name them. `about` is the v1 name of `to`, accepted so that a v1 writer's value is a v2 value unchanged; a value carries one of the two, and v3 drops `about` once every writer sends `to`. Links are read back from the record, never written into the facets an edge names: a facet's read shows the live edges touching it as a derived part beside its payload.

id.description: The edge's own id, chosen once by whoever writes it, and kept for every later version. In a records file the convention is note:<first 8 of the first facet id>:<n>, n counting the person's notes that start there from 1, so a second note is a second fact and not an edit of the first. A conversation writer derives it from the moment and the words, conversation:<16 hex of their sha256>, so the same words said once are one note however often they are sent. A model's reading (card 158) derives it from the note version it read and the fact it wrote.

at.description: The moment the edge was asserted, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM in Australia/Sydney: for a note, when it was written. This is the fact time; the facets the edge names are reached through `from` and `to`, each at its own fact time.

kind.description: What the join means, from a closed list; absent means `about`, which every v1 value is. `about`: the person's words about the facets in `to`, no `from`, `text` required in practice. `interpreted_from` (card 158): the draft facts in `from` were a model's reading of the note versions in `to`, the versions pinned in `pins`, the model's reasoning in `text`. A new kind is a new version of this Definition, added when it has a writer.

from.description: The facet ids on the edge's from side, as the inspector shows them, one or more, or absent. What the side means is the kind's to say. A facet id is stable across the facet's versions, so the edge follows each facet through supersession; Anam does not check that an id is live when the edge is admitted.

to.description: The facet ids on the edge's to side: for a note, the facets it is about, one or more, or absent when it names none yet. The v1 name of this field is `about`; a value carries one of the two names, not both.

about.description: The v1 name of `to`, accepted so that a value written to v1 is a v2 value unchanged. A v2 writer sends `to`; a value with both is refused; v3 drops this field.

pins.description: The exact version of a named facet, where it matters: the facet id to the content hash of the version the edge was asserted against, as sha256:<hex>. For card 158's reading of a note version. A facet id here is one the edge names in `from` or `to`; nothing is pinned unless said.

text.description: The words, verbatim, as the person typed or said them; for a model's reading, its reasoning. Absent on an edge that is only a join.
examples: During a large work meeting, presenting.
